Flight Stick chapter I

3d printed flight stick of the aircraft

CategoryCategory
Date2026-08-13
This flight stick is buit to fly the aircraft called the "F/A-18c Lot-20" in a simulator called "DCS" (Digital combat simulator). The focus was to design and build a flight stick that resembles the real one.

V1.1

Movement

In the stick base are two bearings allinged in the pitch axis. Than there is a subassembly which consists of a square part with two pins, these later get inserted into the two bearings. In the square assembly are two more bearings alligned in the roll axis. The handle is than connected to a tube, which is connected to the bearings alligned in the roll axis.

To add resistance to pitch and roll, each axis has and excenter (the small purple part) and a scissor mechanism. The scissors to add pitch resistance are connected to the stick base. The scissors for roll resistance are connected to the square subassebly. Each scissor pair is connected to eachother with a tention spring

Electronics

To get the pitch and roll angels to DCS, both axes are connected to a potentiometer. They give an analog output to an arduino leonardo (a small computer). The arduino than converts the potentiometer output into angels using a Code.

c++

v1 (first ever code)

Gemini is used to write the code

The code also includes digital inputs (button input) to add further function e.g. a trigger to fire the guns

Flaws

the flight stick felt way to light. The tention springs were way to weak. The motion also didn't feel smooth

v1.4.1

Fixes

To fix the flaws of the first version the scissors where replaced with bigger and more sturdier once to withstand the bigger force of the stronger tention springs. The bearing mounts on both assemblies also have been made more sturdier. To make the motion smoother, bigger bearings have been added (they poke out a bit).

Added features

In the version before the buttons were very simplified by using push buttons only. They were updated by replacing three of them by "castle switches". These are switches that are able to be pushed to the left/right or up/down. In the image shown as crosses with four different functions in each direction.

Problem with inputs

As seen in the image the arduino only has 12 digital inputs. Instead of the 16 inputs needed. This problem is hoever easy to solve by using two extention cards, each having 8 digital inputs. The code has than to be adjusted to be able to use the extention cards.

Open hornet

The flight stick design came from the Openhornet build package: Openhornet. A few things had to be changed. The original designed used a lot of different screw types. They where reduced to only a few crew types. The stick handle beeing used was the thrustmaster f-18 handle. To attach the custom handel it had to be clamped onto the aluminium tube. 

Pitch

This is the last version (v2) of the flight stick. It uses a spring-damper system for the pitch axis. The spring subassebly is made up by two parts (the parts surrounding the spring in blue). These parts are sliding along two 8mm rods using sintered bearings on the left and right. The 8mm rods have each a adjusting ring on the ends to stop the sliding part to slide of. In the middle of the spring runs another 8mm rod which goes all the way into the big blue part. At the end of the middle rod is an adjusting ring. If the pilot pushes the stick forward The rod in the middle gets pulled forward. Because there is a adjusting ring on the end it pulls the slinding part with it. Because the sliding part in the front is at a stop the spring gets compressed. If the pilot pulls on the stick the rod in the middle gets pushed back. Because theres another adjusting ring it pushes on the front sliding part. Because the rear sliding part is at a stop the compression spring gets compressed. As seen in the video 

Roll

The scissor set up is the same as in v1. The only changes are that the scissors are made out of metal. The tension spring has been change to stronger ones and in the old version there was only one spring connecting the scissors. Now they get connected by three springs
